packages/core/src/account/index.ts.description: The account part of the accounts core: what an account keeps, the registry, sessions and passwords.

packages/core/src/account/model.ts.description: What an account is, kept as little as works: a local id, an optional name the person chose, and the ways they sign in. A provider's own id for the person is never kept as it came; it is kept as a keyed hashPassword, so the sealed file can match a sign-in without holding who the person is at that provider.

packages/core/src/account/password.ts.description: Passwords: a person may give an account a password, so they can sign in on this computer without a provider or an magic link (the private-email way in). Only a scrypt password hash is kept, and wrong tries pause sign-in for a while. How hard the hash is to make, how long a password must be, how many wrong tries pause it and for how long are all the owner's numbers.

functions.name: verifyPassword
functions.returns: { readonly result: Result<true>; readonly next: PasswordState }

packages/core/src/account/registry.ts.description: The accounts on this computer: signing in with a checked identity or a password, making an account the first time, joining and removing sign-ins, naming and removing an account. Everything is kept in the product's sealed store, every change is recorded first, and only a person makes a change.

packages/core/src/account/sessions.ts.description: Sessions: once a person has signed in, the product holds a session token so they are not asked again until it ends. The token is shown to the product once; the store keeps only its SHA-256, so the sealed file cannot be used to sign in.

packages/core/src/base/actor.ts.description: Who is acting, and the clock. Every change to an account (making it, joining or removing a sign-in, removing the account, turning telemetry on or off) is a person's: an in-app assistant may read and type, never decide.

packages/core/src/base/codes.ts.description: The accounts code catalogue: every code the core package gives, in plain words a person can read. A code never carries an email address, a provider's subject, a session token or a password.

packages/core/src/base/index.ts.description: The base part of the accounts core: results, the code catalogue, owner settings, who is acting and the clock.

packages/core/src/base/result.ts.description: A result and its issues: every expected failure is returned, never thrown, so a caller sees every problem at once. The shape is the same as Poly's kernel (`{ ok, value }` or `{ ok, issues }`), so a product's own store or record that returns Poly results fits the ports here without a wrapper.

packages/core/src/base/settings.ts.description: The owner's settings: every number the accounts module needs (how long a session lasts, how hard a password is to guess, how many wrong tries pause sign-in) comes from the deployment. Nothing is chosen here; unset refuses.

packages/core/src/index.ts.description: Accounts core: accounts kept on the person's own computer, sealed through the product's store, with sessions, passwords and an audit log of every change. Only a person changes an account.

packages/core/src/local/conformance.ts.description: The store check a product runs against its own vault before it hands it to the accounts module: it proves the store keeps a copy, gives back exactly what it was given, replaces whole, lists and removes, and refuses what it cannot hold, without the module ever seeing how the store seals.

packages/core/src/local/documents.ts.description: Documents in the sealed store, and the audit log around every change: accounts, sessions and settings are kept as JSON, one sealed item each, and every change is written to the audit log before it is made.

packages/core/src/local/index.ts.description: The local part of the accounts core: the ports to the product's vault and audit log, documents in the store, the store check a product runs on its own vault, and the SIMULATED stand-ins.

packages/core/src/local/memory.ts.description: SIMULATED stand-ins for tests and demonstrations: a store that keeps items in memory (it seals nothing, so it is never used for a person's real account) and a hash-chained audit log in memory.

packages/core/src/local/port.ts.description: The two things the accounts module needs from the product it runs in: a sealed store on the person's computer, and an audit log to append to. The module seals nothing itself; it uses the product's own vault, so there is one way keys are kept, not two.

packages/email/src/flow/index.ts.description: The flow part of email sign-in: the owner settings, signing in by link, and email with a password.

packages/email/src/flow/magic-links.ts.description: Signing in with a magic link: the person types their address, an email with a one-time link is sent, and opening the link on this computer signs them in, making the account the first time. The answer to asking for a link never says whether an account exists for the address.

packages/email/src/flow/password.ts.description: The private-email way in without links: an account named by the person's email address and kept by a password, on this computer only. The address is not verified this way, and the account says so; opening a magic link for the same address later reaches the same account.

packages/email/src/flow/settings.ts.description: The owner's settings for magic links, read all at once so the owner sees every missing one together. Email links are optional: they are off until the owner turns them on for a deployment, and a person may still choose a password instead.

packages/email/src/index.ts.description: Email sign-in: the private-email way in, by password on this computer or by optional one-time links.

packages/email/src/link/address.ts.description: Email addresses for the private-email way in: one form for every address, so the same person typing their address twice, in two cases, reaches one account. And the email package's code catalogue.

packages/email/src/link/index.ts.description: The link part of email sign-in: addresses and the code catalogue, link tokens and where links open, the store of links sent.

packages/email/src/link/store.ts.description: The store of magic links sent and not yet used: each link works once, until it ends, and only for the address it was sent to. How long a link lasts is the owner's number.

packages/email/src/link/token.ts.description: Sign-in link tokens and the links that carry them: a link opens the product on the person's own computer, where the token is redeemed once. Where links open is the owner's setting, and only places an app on the person's computer may be opened at are allowed.

packages/email/src/mail/index.ts.description: The mail part of email sign-in: the mail sender port and the SIMULATED outbox, the words of the email, the send limit.

packages/email/src/mail/message.ts.description: The words of a sign-in email: plain text, no images, no tracking, no links but the one sign-in link, and the time it ends. The product's name is the owner's setting, so no product is named here.

packages/email/src/mail/port.ts.description: How a sign-in email leaves the computer: through a mail sender the product plugs in. The accounts module sends nothing itself. A real sender is a connector in connectors-lib, chosen and turned on by the owner; until then the SIMULATED outbox keeps messages in memory.

packages/email/src/mail/rate-limit.ts.description: How many sign-in links one address may be sent in a while, so the product cannot be used to flood someone's inbox. Both numbers are the owner's.

packages/email/test/email.test.ts.description: Tests of email sign-in: addresses, where links open, the email's words, the send limit, the link store, signing in by link and by email with a password. SIMULATED: the outbox keeps messages in memory; synthetic `.test` people.

packages/telemetry/src/consent/consent.t.description: Consent, per person and per probe: off until the person turns it on, for that probe's version only, and turning it off deletes what was counted for them. Only a person changes it.

packages/telemetry/src/consent/counts.ts.description: Each person's counts: what the meter added for them, by export interval and probe, kept in the vault until it is exported or they say no.

packages/telemetry/src/consent/index.ts.description: The consent part of telemetry: consent per person per probe, and the meter that counts only with it.

packages/telemetry/src/consent/meter.ts.description: The meter: hands each local event to every probe the person said yes to, and adds what comes back to their counts for the current export interval. Nothing is counted for a person who has not said yes, or while telemetry is off.

packages/telemetry/src/export/batches.ts.description: Builds export batches: the counts of every ended export interval, added up across everyone on this computer, with small counts suppressed so that no one person's behaviour can be read from a batch.

packages/telemetry/src/export/exporter.t.description: The metric exporter port, where an export batch goes, and the simulated exporter that stands in for it. A product plugs in its own exporter (the owner's choice of service, through a connector); until then nothing leaves.

packages/telemetry/src/export/index.ts.description: The export part of telemetry: the exporter port, the batches and the person-approved export.

packages/telemetry/src/export/telemetry-.description: Exporting counts: a person sees exactly what would be sent, sends it, and can read the history of every batch sent from this computer. Only a person sends; an assistant cannot.

packages/telemetry/src/index.ts.description: Accounts telemetry: disclosed, aggregate-only counts from probes (adapter-lib), kept only for people who said yes and sent only when a person sends them.

packages/telemetry/src/probe/adapter-lib.description: Types for the telemetry probe contract and the shared probes, which adapter-lib ships as plain JavaScript (no build step, no types).

packages/telemetry/src/probe/disclosure..description: What a person is shown before they choose whether a probe may count: what it collects, why, what it never collects, and every count it can make. As data for a screen, and as plain text for a printout or an export.

packages/telemetry/src/probe/registry.ts.description: The probes a product runs, each checked against the probe contract before it is taken, and the telemetry codes.

tools/code-map.mjs.description: The code map: `codemap.json` holds one map per code file (description, features, address, keys, imports, exports, classes with their methods, interfaces, types, functions, constants, tests and dependencies); the feature map (`feature-map.json`, which files carry each feature and which address each holds) and its readable twin (`features.md`). `--check` fails when any of the three is out of date, a code file has no `@feature` or one not in `repo.json`, a file is longer than `repo.json` → `maxLines`, or a package breaks the 1x3xn shape.

tools/docs.mjs.description: The document exports: every document a person reads, as Word (.docx, which Google Docs opens), PDF and plain text.

tools/features-md.mjs.description: The readable feature list, `features.md`: each feature with what it covers, the files that carry it (with their one-line descriptions and line counts) and the addresses it holds, written from the same data as `feature-map.json`.

tools/keys.mjs.description: The key check: every test name starts with its key (one of repo.json → testKeyPrefixes), every key is listed once in the key registry against the file that holds it, and every listed key is still a test.

tools/markers.mjs.description: The internal-words check: none of the words in `repo.json` → `internalMarkers` appears in anything a person can read, which here is every code's plain words (`says: '…'`), every package's description and every document.
